dedupe_keys.name: open energy ontology oeo controlled vocabulary for energy system modelling

description: The Open Energy Ontology (OEO) is a dynamic domain ontology for energy system modelling, developed within the Open Energy Family led by the Reiner Lemoine Institut and updated on a release cycle; the page points to version 2.13.0. It is a structured collection of terms and relationships that gives energy modellers a common language, with clear definitions that disambiguate terms, support data annotation and integration, templates for uniform data capture, visualisation and text and data mining across resources. Every entity is reachable through its IRI on an entity detail page, and an extended module, OEOX, adds post-coordinated terms for complex energy-related concepts. Development began in the SzenarienDB project and continued in LOD_GEOSS, SEDOS, Stadt-Land-Energie and SIROP. Coverage is global and sector-neutral across electricity, gas, heat and fuels. Access: an online viewer and search, an ontology course, and a community repository on GitHub for contributions. Licence and cost: free, with a CC0-1.0 SPDX header on the page. Caveats: a vocabulary, not a dataset, so its value depends on adoption in data and model documentation. It suits harmonising model inputs and metadata, and relates to the Open Energy Platform record catalogued here.
